transcript.text: LG F4V5VYP0W says OE and the clothes are sat in water. I'm not opening the little door at the bottom because last time I did that it flooded the whole kitchen. What else can I do?

I have noted the OE code on your LG display; this next step is the right place to start regardless of your preference regarding the drain filter. Before proceeding, please ensure that no water has reached the plug or socket—if it has, do not touch it and tell me straight away. Also, remember that the door will stay locked until all the water has gone, so do not try to force it open. Next, run a drain or spin-only programme and listen near the bottom front of the machine while it tries to pump out. Does the water pump away, and can you hear the pump humming or is it silent?
No, the water stays in the drum. I can hear the pump humming, and there's an occasional rattle too. Nothing's got near the plug as far as I can see.

Thanks for sharing those details about the pump noise and water remaining in the drum. Before we look at the drain hose at the back of the machine, please switch it off and unplug it first. The appliance is heavy and may still hold water, so ease it forward carefully, ideally with help. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Do not disconnect the hose while there is still water in the machine. Once safe to proceed, check for kinks or crushing on the hose and inspect where it enters the standpipe or sink waste. Was the hose clear, did you find and clear a kink or blockage, or is there one you can't clear?
Right, I pulled it out a bit and the hose was squashed behind it because the machine is pushed right back against the wall. I've straightened it out. Want me to try a spin again?

Now that the blockage is cleared, let's test it: run a drain or spin-only programme. If any water has reached the plug or socket, don't touch it — tell me straight away instead. The door will stay locked until the water has gone, so don't try to force it open. Does the water pump away now?
I tried the spin again. It drained a little slower than normal, but then it showed OE again and the water's still in there.

[Heading: Blocked pump filter]
Thanks for letting us know that the water remains in the drum and the cycle did not pump it out. From what we've been able to check, the most likely cause is a blockage in the pump filter. An appliance engineer is the best next step to confirm it.
